_note: PLACEHOLDER campaign AI tuning (docs/ai-design.md). Every number is a tunable placeholder, not approved balance. The AI acts only through the same functions as the player (no bonus gold, free units or ignored movement/upkeep); these weights only steer its choices. core/ai.gd applies them.

power._note: Cheap strength estimate used to screen threats and opportunities. Unit power = men x (melee_attack + melee_defence + armour x armour_weight + charge x charge_weight + missile damage x volleys x missile_weight) / divisor x (1 + rank x rank_bonus). Settlement defence = automatic garrison + garrisoned armies + friendly armies within reinforcement range x reinforce_share, all x (1 + wall_bonus) when walled.

reach._note: An army can threaten or strike targets within reach_meters straight-line distance (about one turn's 60 movement points at mixed terrain cost). war_meters: how far a faction looks for targets when choosing a war and where to march (a few turns). Movement.plan confirms the chosen action; plan_candidates caps how many targets per army are path-checked per turn (A* is the expensive part).

odds._note: Battle odds. A power ratio (own / enemy) above sure_ratio or below hopeless_ratio decides without simulating; between them the AI runs odds_runs seeded fast simulations (Battles.odds, the same estimate the player's balance bar uses, with fewer runs; about 3 ms each in the debug build). At most odds_budget such estimates per faction per turn; beyond that the win chance is read off a logistic curve 1 / (1 + exp(-curve_k x (ratio - 1))).

attack._note: Attack an army or settlement when the estimated win chance is at least min_odds (divided by the personality's boldness). An army at war with nothing in reach marches on the best target within war_meters whose power ratio is at least march_ratio (divided by boldness). A walled settlement is besieged instead unless the assault odds reach assault_min_odds; it is besieged only when the army's power is at least siege_ratio (divided by boldness) of the defenders' power without the wall bonus, i.e. when it could beat them in the open and hold the siege lines. Besieging armies hold their siege.

defend._note: A settlement is threatened when the power of enemy (and wary-of) armies within threat_meters exceeds its defence x threatened_ratio. Armies within reach move in to defend if together they reach save_ratio of the threat; otherwise they do not sacrifice themselves. In a field battle the defender withdraws when its odds are below withdraw_below (garrisons cannot withdraw). An army facing a threat above flee_ratio x its own power with no help falls back to its nearest own settlement.

war._note: Declaring war on a faction not yet at war (temporary rule: attacking declares war). Each turn, for its best opportunity against a faction it is at peace with, a faction declares with chance base_chance x aggression x weakness, where weakness = min(2, score) - 1 (0 when not stronger); score = the power of its field armies within war_meters x gather_share (or the attacking army's own ratio, if higher) / target defence; for a walled settlement siege_weight x that ratio without walls when higher (a target it could besiege). The same force ratio decides whether armies march on a target. max_wars caps simultaneous wars it starts (wars never end yet: no peace exists). The faction must also pass the attack odds test for the target itself.

economy._note: Construction. Keep reserve_gold (x personality reserve) in the treasury, and net income after new upkeep at least min_net_income. Safe: build by economy_weights; threatened: by threatened_weights. Weight = category weight x personality multiplier; ties by cheapest, then settlement id. max_builds_per_turn per faction.

recruitment._note: Armies recruit toward a target composition (shares of each role; role of a unit: levy if peasant_levy, else spear if it braces, else its category). The unit with the largest shortfall among those available, affordable (above the reserve) and within upkeep is queued; max_recruits_per_turn per army. A faction raises a new army when under its army target (base_armies x personality armies, capped by the faction army cap) and it can pay the general plus raise_margin gold above its reserve; a faction with no army at all only keeps emergency_reserve_share of its reserve, and so does recruiting while the faction has fewer than garrison_units units in all. garrison_units: a home army aims for at least this many units before it is sent out. field_units: the usual army size; a faction with more than rich_factor x its reserve fills armies up to the army cap instead.

grace._note: A landless faction in its grace period (core/realm.gd) puts everything into retaking a settlement: boldness x boldness (attacks at worse odds), aggression at least 1, war declared on the owner of its best reachable settlement target without a roll, only settlements targeted, and no siege that would outlast its grace.

presentation._note: End Turn on the map (main.gd): AI armies whose path comes within watch_meters of the player's settlements or armies are shown one at a time, the camera following at most camera_distance away and holding hold_seconds after each arrives (Settings: follow AI movements Off / Only near my territory / All, default Off; AI turn speed 1x/2x/4x divides the hold; Space or Esc skips). Presentation only: it never changes what the AI did.

personalities._note: Multipliers per trait (faction traits in data/factions.json, from docs/archive/world-v1.md); a faction's value is the product over its traits. aggression scales the war chance; boldness divides attack.min_odds (bolder = attacks at worse odds); reserve scales the gold reserve; armies scales the army target; economy scales the weight of economic buildings; defense scales defense/military building weight; wariness = how much other factions treat this one's armies as threats before war (AI-internal; not a relationship value, which stays open); assault: 1 prefers assault to siege; vengeful: always at war with whoever attacked it; opportunist: prefers targets already at war with someone else; composition overrides the recruitment shares.
